messages:
jasper: Quick RFC follow-up — thanks for the reviews. TL;DR: propose we move from tunnelled hedging (global hedges at fixed pct) to a latency-led budget model that spends a per-route 'hedge budget' tied to observed probe staleness and regional grace windows. opens with high-level tradeoffs and then concrete rollouts.

maya: Can you sketch the budget lifecycle? is that per-tenant or per-route?

jasper: per-route to start (route = customer+model+tier). budget is a moving token bucket that accrues credits when latency is under SLO and drains when we hedged. credits cap tied to route commit tier. This keeps enterprise customers from unlimited cost while allowing transient extra hedges.

liam: Sounds good. How do probes feed into this? we saw oscillation when probe signal lags.

jasper: Good point — core idea: decouple probe-derived penalty from immediate hedge decision. We compute two signals: fast-probe (last-10s p90) and stable-probe (last-5min p90). Hedge action only if fast-probe crosses threshold AND stable-probe confirms or hedge-budget is non-zero. That avoids flip-flop from brief probe noise.

priya: Agree on two signals. We also need to handle region failovers where probes go stale due to partition. propose a 'grace window' per region: a short timer (default 30s) after probe loss where we prefer fallback models but don't immediately punish capacity.

sam: 30s seems fine as default but we need per-tenant override for regulated customers. also, what about skew across similar routes — i.e., many small routes in same region all hedging at once and consuming shared capacity?

jasper: We'll add an optional affinity key so related routes can be grouped. Group-level soft cap prevents thundering hedges. By default group = region:tenant.

ana-ml: From the runtime side, what contract do you want? runtime needs a simple API: Decide(route, signals, budget_state) -> Action {serve, hedge_to_variant, fallback_region}. Keep the policy evaluation deterministic and cheap. Also we should version the decision proto.

jasper: Exactly — policy contract v1: inputs are route_id, model_family, fast_probe_ms, stable_probe_ms, budget_tokens, active_affinity_group. Output action + budget_delta + reason_code. We'll add a human-readable explain string for ops.

will (eng-sre): Ops note: we must emit telemetry for budget_tokens over time and hedge count per minute per region. Otherwise cost surprises will bite us. Also add a kill-switch for global hedging.

devx: One UX ask: show per-route hedge budget and recent probe staleness in Console (tiny sparkline + why we hedged). helps SREs.

priya: Rollout plan? we should canary to a shadow mode first where we log actions but don't change runtime behavior. then a 5% hedging canary where we allow budget consumption but with emergency caps.

jasper: Proposed rollout: (1) policy simulator integrated into the sandbox (authors: liam + ana-ml) to validate against traces, (2) shadow roll on dedicated infra for 48h, (3) 5% live canary (configurable per org), (4) scale to 25% with telemetry gating, (5) global release.

sam: What about pricing implications? per-token costs might spike if we hedge a lot. Finance wants predictability.

jasper: We'll expose budget cap settings per-tenant and a monthly 'hedge spend' estimate in billing. Also add an alert when burn rate > x% of forecast.

maya: Implementation notes: policy should live in the policy-compiler repo as a signed policy artifact and the runtime will use a lightweight wasm evaluator to avoid redeploys. That gives us hotpatch.

ana-ml: Keep an eye on perf — wasm evaluator adds ~0.3ms median. acceptable but we must measure p99. If high, fallback to precompiled native path for hot hot routes.

will (eng-sre): Safety: emergency kill-switch should be a central flag that bypasses policy and returns last-known-good routing. Also a route-level 'do not hedge' override for regulated tenants.

devx: UX: create a small Console flow to toggle per-route hedge cap and to opt-out. Also surface the reason_code for each hedged request in traces.

priya: Tests: unit tests for budget accounting, integration tests with synthetic probe jitter, chaos test that kills probes to ensure grace window behaves. We should also add a simulation test that replays a spike and ensures budget burn doesn't exceed configured caps.

liam: Action items?

jasper: I'll open an RFC follow-up that includes the policy proto and rollout checklist. Owners: simulator (liam + ana-ml), runtime contract + wasm stub (ana-ml + devx), console bits (devx), telemetry & alarms (will + sam), billing hooks (sam + finance), canary ops (priya). Target: shadow roll in 3 weeks.

sam: +1 on owners. one more ask: add a retro checkpoint 2 weeks post-25% to validate cost impact.

jasper: agreed. I'll add to checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:
